etymology: Hebrew Elʿazar — “God has helped.” Aaron’s third surviving son after Nadab and Abihu died; the name is a confession, not a family ornament.
biblical_def: Eleazar is the priest who received Aaron’s garments on Mount Hor and kept the charge of the sanctuary after the plague. He is chief over the chief of the Levites (Num 3:32). When Aaron died, Moses stripped Aaron of his garments and put them upon Eleazar his son (Num 20:28). The office did not die with the man. After the plague the LORD spoke to Moses and to Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest (Num 26:1). Help is from God; succession is by His appointment.

etymology: Hebrew Lewi — joined. Leah named the third son for hoped joining to her husband; the LORD later joined the tribe to Himself for ark, ministry, and blessing.
biblical_def: Levi is the third son of Jacob and Leah, and the tribe the LORD separated to bear the ark of the covenant, to stand before the LORD to minister, and to bless in His name (Deu 10:8). Hebrews can say that Levi, who receiveth tithes, paid tithes in Abraham (Heb 7:9) — the lesser in the greater, the tribe inside the patriarch. The name is not a hobby of genealogy. It is the joined people set apart for holy service.

etymology: Greek Simōn, from Hebrew Shimʿon — hearing. Several New Testament men bear it; the chief is Simon called Peter, fisher of Galilee renamed Cephas, a stone.
biblical_def: Simon is first a fisher. Jesus walking by the sea of Galilee saw two brethren, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net (Mat 4:18). He is also named Peter (Luk 6:14). Brought to Jesus, he is told: Thou art Simon the son of Jona: thou shalt be called Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone (Joh 1:42). The name of hearing becomes the name of rock by Christ’s word, not by Simon’s résumé.

etymology: Hebrew Avram — exalted father. The LORD later named him Abraham, father of many nations. Abram is the earlier name of the same man called out of Ur.
biblical_def: Abram is the man the LORD called out of country, kindred, and father’s house unto a land He would shew (Gen 12:1). After these things the word of the LORD came unto Abram in a vision: Fear not, Abram: I am thy shield, and thy exceeding great reward (Gen 15:1). Nehemiah confesses that the LORD chose Abram, brought him forth out of Ur of the Chaldees, and gave him the name of Abraham (Neh 9:7). The change of name is gift, not self-rebranding.

etymology: Hebrew Laban — white. Brother of Rebekah, father of Leah and Rachel, uncle and master of Jacob in Padan-aram. The name is ordinary; the man is a bargainer.
biblical_def: Laban ran out unto the man at the well when Rebekah had a brother (Gen 24:29). He had two daughters, Leah the elder and Rachel the younger (Gen 29:16). Jacob served him fourteen years for the daughters and six for cattle, and Laban changed his wages ten times (Gen 31:41). He is kin who uses kin. Hospitality at the well becomes a house of delayed wages. The story is not a folk comedy of tricksters; it is covenant history under a hard uncle.

etymology: Old English murnan — to grieve, to be anxious. Scripture’s mourning is not a mood board. It is grief under God, timed, commanded, and comforted.
biblical_def: To mourn is to grieve as the blessed do: Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted (Mat 5:4). There is a time to mourn as surely as a time to dance (Ecc 3:4). Isaiah’s Servant is sent to comfort all that mourn (Isa 61:2). Mourning is not unbelief. It is the honest posture of those who still expect comfort from the LORD, not from distraction.

etymology: Hebrew Yishai — possibly “gift” or related to being. Bethlehemite father of David; the stem from which the Branch is said to grow.
biblical_def: Jesse is the Bethlehemite whose son the LORD provided as king when Saul was rejected (the horn of oil is sent to his house). The women of Bethlehem named Obed the father of Jesse, the father of David (Rut 4:17). Isaiah promises a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch out of his roots (Isa 11:1). Matthew records: Jesse begat David the king (Mat 1:6). Jesse is not a rustic extra. He is the named stem of the royal line.

etymology: Hebrew Natan — he has given. Several men bear the name; the prophet Nathan is the giver of the LORD’s word to David — house, sin, and succession.
biblical_def: Nathan the prophet stands in David’s court as the LORD’s mouth. The king said unto Nathan that he dwelt in a house of cedar while the ark dwelt within curtains (2Sa 7:2). Nathan later said unto David, Thou art the man, after the LORD had anointed him and delivered him from Saul (2Sa 12:7). In the succession crisis he is listed with Zadok among those not with Adonijah (1Ki 1:8). A true prophet gives the word even when the king has cedar and blood on his hands.
